newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Spreads marginally tighter.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Spreads marginally tighter.

text.p: *Semi-government bond yield spreads showed a tightening bias, although traders said this was more a result of inaction by semis rather than a concerted outperformance.

Semi-government bond yield spreads showed a tightening bias to Australian Treasury debt in the past week, although traders said this was more as result of inaction by semis rather than a concerted outperformance.
"There has been some interest in global exchangeable bonds, but domestically is pretty much comatosed," one trader added.

Some Japanese selling was evident in short-dated stock at the start of last week as part of a recent switch from Australian dollar assets to higher yield markets, but this appeared to have little sustained impact on semi yield margins.

Semi government issuers were still looking to Japanese investors as one major base to absorb their debt with Queensland Treasury Corp launching a short dated US$250 millon Eurodollar note in Tokyo last week, maturing in March 1998.

New South Wales Treasury Corp (TCorp) also said in its six monthly financial update that it continued to focus on the Japanese retail sector during the December quarter, issuing A$812 million of debt into the Japanese market.
Last week's shake-out in the government bond market amid signs of accelerating growth and a clear indication by the Reserve Bank that policy is on hold pushed semi yields higher.
The RBA also warned in its quarterly Bulletin of its concerns over wages growth, and two elements of this are due to be released in data this week.

Final average weekly oridinary time earnings are due to be released on Thursday, while the latest report from the Department of Industrial Relations on enterprise bargaining agreements is expected to emerge on Wednesday.
However, the outcome of the trade union movement's 8.75 percent "living wage" claim will not be known until next month.
